description: A user's own projects. NOT the scheduler app's `projects` table (507) - that one belongs to the Claude automation system, lives in a different Baserow database, and has no user column. Import TWENTY-SEVENTH (no dependencies)
notes: Named user_projects, not projects, so it can never be confused with the scheduler's table of the same name in the other database.
Users live in Xano, not Baserow, so user_id is TEXT holding String(user.id) - never a link field.

status carries 'cancelled' and 'on_hold' spelled WITHOUT the trailing comma that the scheduler table's option has. Baserow rejects any value outside a single-select's options, so the app's mapper had to reproduce that typo exactly; a clean table means a clean mapping.
priority uses 'urgent' - the word the app actually uses. The scheduler table says 'critical', which needed translating in both directions.
tags is free TEXT (comma separated), not a multiple_select. The scheduler's tags column is limited to bug/feature/improvement/docs, so arbitrary user tags could not be saved at all.
progress is 0-100 and derived by the client from task completion; stored so a list view can show it without loading every task.
Sub-collections (tasks, milestones, goals) are separate tables, not link fields, so a project loads without fanning out.

user_id.description: Xano user id as a string. EVERY read filters on this

tags.description: Comma separated. Free text on purpose - a select would reject anything unplanned
